title: Book Two · Chapter 128: The Hours Sheet
story:
On Saturday, Dad takes Ronan to Mr Sun's counter for a short visit. Mum needs the room at home for a fitting with a customer.

Ronan sits on the visitor's chair. He has a story book. Dad has a work sheet with four jobs on it.

Mr Sun comes from the back room.

“The cabinet first,” he says. “The small box can wait until Monday. Please tell the customer.”

Dad reads the sheet, then looks at the clock.

“The cabinet needs another hour. Maybe more if the bottom is loose.”

“Check first. Then call.”

Dad goes to the back with Mr Sun. Ronan stays by the counter. He opens his book to a picture of a road.

After a few minutes, Dad returns. He writes beside the cabinet line.

“More?” Ronan asks.

“Two hours. The bottom needs a new piece.”

“Will the customer be angry?”

“She may be. I am calling now.”

Ronan looks down at his page while Dad makes the call. Dad tells the customer he needs two more hours. He does not promise to finish sooner.

For a little while, Dad only listens. Ronan can hear a voice from the phone, but he cannot follow the words.

Dad looks at the new mark on his sheet. He answers slowly and leaves time for the customer to speak again.

Ronan opens his story at the road picture. He reads one sentence, then looks back at Dad.

He wants the customer to say it is all right. Dad cannot make her say that.

Dad has written two hours beside the cabinet line. The part that needs work is still at the back.

Dad gives the customer the new time again before he puts the phone down.

Ronan has waited through a long little call. Nobody has touched a tool during it. The work has still changed: the customer knows about the extra time now.

He keeps his own question until Dad has finished with the sheet.

When the call ends, he draws one line through the old finish time. The old time is still visible.

“Why leave the old one?” Ronan asks.

“So we can see the change.”

“Does Mr Sun count it against you?”

“He needs to know how long the job takes.”

Dad turns the sheet. There is space on the back for parts and payments. The new piece has a cost beside it.

“Do you lose money every time something takes longer?”

“Not always. We still need to count the work.”

Mr Sun returns to the counter with a cup. “And sometimes we say no to the next job.”

Dad nods. Ronan thinks about all the jobs a person can want at once.

At noon, Dad has ten minutes to eat. Ronan opens the packet Mum gives them. There are two buns and pieces of cucumber.

Dad bites a bun and points to the story picture.

“Is that man lost?”

“No. He is waiting for a cart.”

Dad leans closer. “I thought that was his hat.”

Ronan shows him the wheel at the side. Dad laughs.

“A large hat.”

Ronan reads the short paragraph aloud. Dad listens while he eats. Then he looks at the clock and stands.

At the door, Ronan checks the route home. Mum has agreed that he can walk the quiet part alone now. He stays on that route. At home, the customer's fitting is over. Mum asks for the empty packet. Ronan gives it to her. He has eaten both cucumber pieces.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

cabinet＝柜子；fitting＝试衣；visible＝看得见的；parts＝零件。

## 理解问题

1. Dad为什么保留被划掉的原时间？
2. 父子怎样在短午饭里分享故事？

## 读句子

**Dad / goes to the back / with Mr Sun.** Dad／到后面去／和Mr Sun一起。
